html:
SMTO-SKL-0044 — SMTO couldn't open the file you want to upload to Drive

GUID: 68c36bae-2f47-5e0a-a31b-5596b092e0d3
Slug: google-drive-upload-source-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO can only upload files saved in this conversation, and it couldn't open the one you chose. It may have come from somewhere else or no longer be available. Nothing was sent to Drive.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to save the file you want to upload as a file in this conversation, naming the computer and folder it is on. SMTO uploads only files saved in the current conversation, not files picked from anywhere on a computer.
  2. If the file was made in a different conversation, ask for the upload in that conversation, or have SMTO save it again here. Each conversation can only use its own saved files.
  3. Then ask SMTO to upload that saved file to Google Drive, and approve the request. With a file SMTO can open, the upload can go ahead safely.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the upload as finished, and the file appears in the Google Drive folder you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the file's contents into the chat as a workaround if it is private.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Upload-source resolution failed: source_ref is not an artifact:// or artifact-workspace:// reference, or opening the conversation-owned artifact raised an artifact, filesystem or missing-metadata error.

What this means

  • Upload-source resolution catches an artifact, filesystem or missing-metadata error while resolving the selected conversation-owned source. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Upload-source resolution catches an artifact, filesystem or missing-metadata error while resolving the selected conversation-owned source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact artifact reference, scope and materialization status before assuming the local file is missing.

How to fix it

  • files.source accepts only artifact://, art_ IDs or artifact-workspace:// refs, and opens them through ArtifactStore.open_stream for the current conversation; ArtifactError, OSError or KeyError map to upload_source_missing. Register the file as a conversation artifact on its source Gateway (artifact.register, or gateway.copy then register) and pass that reference; arbitrary host paths are rejected.
  • Register the file as a conversation artifact on its source Gateway, or use gateway.copy and artifact materialization first. Pass artifact:// or artifact-workspace://; arbitrary host paths are not accepted.

Retry and execution caution

  • Register the file as a conversation artifact on its source Gateway, or use gateway.copy and artifact materialization first. Pass artifact:// or artifact-workspace://; arbitrary host paths are not accepted.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended artifact resolves and its bytes pass integrity checks before upload.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
